title: Bhangui
jainNotes: Contains onion - not consumed by Jains. For Jain version, omit onion.

ingredients.name: Ginger, onion, turmeric, mustard oil or ghee

recipe: Mix rice with grated ginger, onion, turmeric and a little mustard oil or ghee.
Wrap in banana leaves, forming conical or packet shapes, and steam until the rice is cooked and infused with the leaf aroma.
Serve hot – a fragrant traditional rice preparation.
tips: The banana leaf imparts a unique aroma and keeps the rice moist.
Often eaten as a light meal or breakfast.

title: Steamed Rice with Mosdeng Serma
jainNotes: Contains fish (berma) and garlic - not consumed by Jains.

ingredients.name: Berma (fermented dried fish), red chilli, garlic, tomato

recipe: Steam or boil rice. Separately pound or grind berma with red chilli, garlic and tomato into a spicy, pungent chutney (mosdeng serma).
Serve the rice with the mosdeng as a simple, flavourful start to the day.
tips: Mosdeng is the classic Tripuri side – fiery, umami-rich and essential to most meals.
Berma gives the distinctive fermented flavour.

title: Gudok
jainNotes: Contains fermented fish (berma) and onion - not consumed by Jains.

ingredients.name: Seasonal vegetables (potato, beans, pumpkin, bamboo shoot, etc.)

recipe: Boil the vegetables with berma, chilli and salt until soft. Mash everything together into a thick, flavourful mixture.
Garnish with sliced onion. Serve with steamed rice – a staple tribal dish cooked with little or no oil.
tips: Traditional oil-free preparation – the fermented fish provides the main flavour.
Vegetables vary with season and availability.

title: Mui Borok
jainNotes: Contains fermented fish (berma), onion, garlic - not consumed by Jains.

ingredients.name: Seasonal vegetables, bamboo shoot, bottle gourd
Ginger leaves, onion, garlic, green chilli, salt

recipe: Layer or combine vegetables, bamboo shoot and berma with aromatics. Boil or steam until everything is soft and the flavours have melded.
Mash lightly if desired. Serve with rice – often called the soul food of Tripura.
tips: Mui Borok is considered the traditional cuisine of the Tripuri people.
Minimal oil, maximum use of local produce and fermented fish.

title: Chakhwi
jainNotes: Contains onion and garlic - not consumed by Jains. For Jain version, omit onion-garlic.

ingredients.name: Bamboo shoot, banana stem, papaya, other vegetables
Rice paste, alkaline water (khar) or soda, onion, garlic, chilli, salt

recipe: Cook bamboo shoot and other vegetables with a little alkaline water (traditionally extracted from burnt plant ash) and rice paste to thicken.
Season with onion, garlic, chilli and salt. Simmer into a light stew.
Serve with rice – a distinctive Tripuri preparation.
tips: The mild alkaline note is characteristic of traditional Chakhwi.
Bamboo shoot is central.

title: Wahan Mosdeng
jainNotes: Contains pork, onion, garlic - not consumed by Jains.

ingredients.name: Garlic, ginger, green chilli, onion, mustard oil

recipe: Marinate pork with garlic, ginger, chilli and a little mustard oil. Grill, roast or pan-cook until done.
Chop or shred and mix with more fresh chilli, onion and aromatics into a spicy salad-style preparation (mosdeng).
Serve with rice or roti.
tips: Pork salad/bharta – bold, spicy and very popular.
Can also be made with chicken.

title: Mach Bhat (Fish Curry with Rice)
jainNotes: Contains fish, onion, garlic - not consumed by Jains.

ingredients.name: Turmeric, mustard oil, green chilli, onion, ginger, garlic

recipe: Marinate fish with turmeric and salt. Lightly fry or cook in a simple gravy of onion, ginger, garlic, chilli and mustard oil.
Serve with steamed rice – the everyday fish-and-rice meal of the region.
tips: Fish and rice form the cornerstone of daily Tripura diet.
Mustard oil is commonly used.

title: Mwkhwi (Fruit Snack)
jainNotes: Ingredients are Jain-compatible (seasonal fruit, salt, green chilli). No onion, garlic, or root vegetables.
recipe: Cut fresh seasonal fruit into pieces. Toss with salt and crushed green chilli.
Eat as a refreshing, spicy-sweet snack.
tips: Simple fruit preparation popular when mangoes, pineapples or other local fruits are in season.
The chilli-salt combination is classic.

title: Mosdeng (Bamboo Shoot Chutney)
jainNotes: Contains onion and garlic - not consumed by Jains. For Jain version, omit onion-garlic.

ingredients.name: Red or green chilli, garlic, onion, salt

recipe: Pound or grind bamboo shoot with chilli, garlic and salt into a coarse chutney.
Mix in chopped onion. Serve as a side or snack with rice cakes or puffed rice.
tips: Mosdeng variations are endless – bamboo shoot versions are especially popular.
Pungent and addictive.

title: Awandru (Vegetarian Bamboo Shoot Gravy)
jainNotes: Contains onion and garlic - not consumed by Jains. For Jain version, omit onion-garlic.

ingredients.name: Onion, garlic, chilli, salt, coriander for garnish

recipe: Cook bamboo shoot with onion, garlic, chilli and rice flour into a light gravy.
Simmer till the flavours blend. Garnish with fresh herbs.
Serve with rice.
tips: Vegetarian bamboo-shoot based gravy common in Tripuri cooking.
Thickened with rice flour instead of fish.

title: Awandru with Berma (Non-Vegetarian)
jainNotes: Contains fermented fish (berma) and onion - not consumed by Jains.

ingredients.name: Onion, chilli, salt, coriander for garnish

recipe: Cook bamboo shoot with berma, onion and chilli into a light gravy.
Simmer till the flavours blend. Garnish with fresh herbs.
Serve with rice.
tips: Traditional non-vegetarian bamboo-shoot gravy thickened with berma.
The fermented fish adds a deep, umami richness.

title: Pork with Bamboo Shoot
jainNotes: Contains pork, onion, garlic - not consumed by Jains.

ingredients.name: Green chilli, ginger, garlic, onion, salt

recipe: Cook pork with ginger, garlic, onion and chilli until tender. Add bamboo shoot and continue cooking till the flavours meld.
Serve with steamed rice – a hearty tribal favourite.
tips: Bamboo shoot cuts through the richness of the pork.
Fermented bamboo shoot adds extra tang.

title: Khoi / Puffed Rice Snack
jainNotes: Contains onion - not consumed by Jains. For Jain version, omit onion.

ingredients.name: Mustard oil, onion, green chilli, salt

recipe: Toss puffed rice with a little mustard oil, chopped onion, green chilli and salt.
Eat immediately as a light, crunchy snack.
tips: Simple everyday snack across the region.
Can be dressed up with more vegetables or berma for extra flavour.
